paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:1 [additional supplied locator ט.], [his maidservant; supplied שפתחו] passed a synagogue and saw a teacher of young children beating a child excessively. She said, ‘Let this man be excommunicated.’ He came to Rabbi Acha, who told him, ‘You must be concerned for yourself.’

notes.text: The source has שפתחו, apparently a transposition of שפחתו (“his maidservant”); the English brackets that proposal. The masculine “he came” appears to refer to the excommunicated teacher.

The saved whole Venice JerusalemTalmudMoedKatan3:1 scalar names Bar Pata’s maidservant, the excessive beating and the teacher’s inquiry to full Rabbi Acha. It supports the corrected male inquirer and bracketed maidservant, not the earlier female-inquirer rendering. Supplied שפתחו remains a source question, not proof of a printed transposition. Additional locator ט. is retained literally; this digital paragraph does not establish the earlier asserted9a pagination. Bar Pata receives no new personal title.

Printed Hyman (vol. I, p. 287) reads שפחתו, “his maidservant,” and includes the additional ט. The supplied transcription has שפתחו. Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:1 names the maidservant of Bar Pata and has the teacher ask Rabbi Acha after she declares the ban. The episode falls on Vilna 11a in the consulted digital pagination. Hyman’s own additional page marker remains unexplained.
